---
title: "Offline use"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Firewalled analysis environments, common in regulated (GxP) settings, can't
download anything while a report is being set up or built. quartifyr works
there as long as what it would have downloaded is already on the machine. This
page lists what needs the network, how to provide each piece locally, and what
quartifyr cannot fix because it happens in a dependency.

## What needs the network

Only setup does. Rendering a report makes no network calls of its own.

| Step | Why it reaches the network | Offline replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python packages for `render_report()`'s styling steps | pyro runs `uv lock` and `uv sync` | `UV_OFFLINE=1` with a pre-populated cache or wheel directory, or `python_env` |
| Installing `uv` | pyro downloads and installs it into `~/.local/bin` when it is missing | install `uv` yourself |
| The `quarto-plus` Quarto extension | `quarto add` fetches from GitHub | `install_quarto_extensions()`, which has a copy bundled |
| Templates with `from_repo` | `git clone` | clone elsewhere, use `from_dir` |

## Offline mode

Set `options(quartifyr.offline = TRUE)` (or uv's own `UV_OFFLINE=1`, which
quartifyr also honours) and `initialize_quartifyr_project()` changes how it
behaves:

* pyro's provisioning runs with `UV_OFFLINE=1`, so uv resolves from its cache
  or from `UV_FIND_LINKS` wheels instead of PyPI;
* if `uv` isn't installed it stops with a message saying so. Without this, pyro's
  setup script would download uv from GitHub and install it into
  `~/.local/bin`;
* the installed uv's own version is passed to pyro, so a version mismatch can't
  be treated as a reason to download a different one;
* `from_repo` is refused, with a pointer to `from_dir`.

Whenever a step that needs the network fails, the error says which step, which
resource it was after and how to provide it locally. The error class is
`quartifyr_offline_failure`, and it includes uv's own stderr (pyro otherwise
hides it).

## Recipe

While you still have network access, on a machine that matches the target
(same OS and Python version), fill uv's cache and collect the wheels:

```bash
# Installs the packages into uv's cache as a side effect.
uv pip install --python .venv python-docx pyyaml

# Or keep the wheels in a directory you can copy across.
pip download --dest wheels python-docx pyyaml
```

Then, on the firewalled machine:

```{r}
options(quartifyr.offline = TRUE)

# Point uv at the wheels if you aren't using its cache, and skip the index.
Sys.setenv(UV_FIND_LINKS = "/path/to/wheels", UV_NO_INDEX = "1")

# The bundled quarto-plus and quartifyr's own extension install with no
# network, and so does Python provisioning.
quartifyr::initialize_quartifyr_project(
  "report-project",
  install_extensions = TRUE,
  from_dir = "/path/to/templates"   # optional: an org template, already cloned
)
```

`install_quarto_extensions()` can also install a different copy of an
extension, such as a version your site has vetted, from a directory or a
`.zip`/`.tar.gz` archive: `install_quarto_extensions(path, from = "quarto-plus.zip")`.

### An existing Python environment

If you would rather not use uv on that machine at all, point quartifyr at an
environment that already has `python-docx` and `pyyaml`:

```{r}
quartifyr::initialize_quartifyr_project("report-project", python_env = "/opt/envs/quartifyr")
```

The environment is checked, and a missing module is named along with the
package to install. Nothing in the project is touched. Put the same setting in
the project's `.Rprofile` so `render_report()` uses it too:

```{r}
options(quartifyr.python_env = "/opt/envs/quartifyr")
```

The `QUARTIFYR_PYTHON_ENV` environment variable works as well. The
`quartifyr_styling` module itself doesn't need installing: the copy bundled in
the R package is put on `PYTHONPATH`.

## Not covered

`reportifyr`, which fills the shell in pass 2, has its own Python environment
and provisions it through pyro and uv when you call
`reportifyr::initialize_report_project()`. That code is upstream (A2-ai), and
`python_env` does not replace it. It works offline under the same conditions as
above: uv installed at any version, `UV_OFFLINE=1`, and a populated cache or
wheel directory. If a step in it needs the network, the error comes from
there, not from quartifyr.

## The `quarto-plus` licence

`A2-ai/quarto-plus` is MIT-licensed (Copyright (c) 2024 Posit Software, PBC).
Bundling it is allowed so long as its copyright and permission notice stay with
the copy, which is why its `LICENSE` is kept inside the bundled directory and
installed with it into `_extensions/A2-ai/quarto-plus/`. The bundled files are
unmodified upstream at a recorded commit (see `inst/extensions/README.md`), and
`scripts/sync_demo_extension.py --check` fails if the examples' copies drift
from them.

## How this is tested

The `offline-pipeline` CI job provisions the demo project online, then runs
`scripts/offline_pipeline_check.sh` inside a network namespace with no network
interface and an empty `HOME`. It initializes and renders the demo (once with
uv, once with `python_env`) and fails if anything needs the network or writes
to `~/.local/bin`. The same script can be run by hand on Linux; the header of
the script shows how.
